title: Crocs FY2026 Q3 Earnings Call
contentEn:
Operator
Good day, and welcome to the Crocs Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. All participants will be in listen only mode. Should you need assistance, please signal a conference specialist by pressing the star key followed by zero. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your touch-tone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star and then two. Also, please note this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Elizabeth Bouquard Pizzi, Vice President in Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Elizabeth Bouquard Pizzi
Good morning, and thank you for joining us to discuss Crocs, Inc.'s third quarter 2026 results. With me today are Andrew Rees, Chief Executive Officer, and Patraic Reagan, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Following their prepared remarks, we will open the call for your questions, which we ask that you limit to one per caller. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the information provided on this call is forward-looking and accordingly is subject to the safe harbor provisions of the federal securities laws. These statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors which may cause our actual results, performance, or achievements to differ materially. Please refer to our most recent annual report on Form 10-K, quarterly report on Form 10-Q, and other reports filed with the SEC for more information on these risks and uncertainties. Certain financial metrics that we refer to as adjusted or non-GAAP are non-GAAP measures. A reconciliation of these amounts to their GAAP counterparts is contained in the press release we issued earlier this morning. All revenue growth rates will be cited on a constant currency basis unless otherwise stated. At this time, I'll turn the call over to Andrew Rees, Crocs' Chief Executive Officer.

Andrew Rees
Thank you, Elizabeth, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Before I share our results for the third quarter, I'd like to welcome Elizabeth in her new role as Vice President of Investor Relations. We're excited to welcome her as part of our Crocs team. Now moving to our third quarter results. We delivered a strong quarter of growth across brands, channels, and geographies. Both Crocs and HEYDUDE delivered growth driven by execution of our brand strategies while expanding margins year over year through sustained operational discipline. This quarter marks an important inflection for the HEYDUDE brand, with revenue growth of 6%, which is a direct result of our clear consumer focus and execution against our three-pillar growth strategy. The Crocs brand had a record third quarter up 4%, driven by our international business, including growth in all of our tier 1 international markets and continued momentum across our product diversification strategy. As we stated at the beginning of the year, returning to growth for both brands is a strategic goal we set out to achieve through our disciplined execution and laser focus on the consumer. As a result, we are raising our full year 2026 revenue guidance from up 1%-2% to up approximately 3%. We remain confident in the long-term trajectory of both of our brands and are committed to executing against our strategic pillars to drive diversified growth. Additionally, we remain confident in our ability to generate significant free cash flow, which we continue to return to shareholders in the form of meaningful share repurchases and debt paydown. While Patraic will discuss our quarterly performance in more detail later, I will start by sharing several financial highlights and then review our progress by brand. During the third quarter, we delivered enterprise revenues of more than $1 billion, up 5% to prior year, driven by both of our brands, with Crocs up 4% and HEYDUDE up 6%. HEYDUDE returned to growth led by wholesale revenues up 14% and DTC revenues up slightly. Crocs brand delivered a better-than-expected Q3 led by international revenue up double digits, including our international direct-to-consumer channel growing 24%. Another quarter of best-in-class profitability with adjusted operating margins expanding 150 basis points to reach 22.3%. Meaningful return of cash to shareholders with approximately 2 million shares repurchased for $250 million and debt paydown of $21 million. Importantly, over the last decade, we have taken our powerful value creation engine and returned meaningful cash to shareholders with approximately $3 billion of share repurchases and 37% reduction in share count. We view this as a true differentiator versus our peers. Now let's move to performance by brand, starting with Crocs. This quarter was another great quarter for the Crocs brand, reflecting strong execution against our five-pillar growth strategy. Direct-to-consumer revenues grew 8% versus prior year, led by our international business, while our diversification strategy continued to gain traction with consumers. We built on the momentum established in the first half of the year, driven by strong consumer response to our new product innovation, impactful partnerships, and our differentiated digitally led approach to commerce and marketing. Turning to our five-pillar growth strategy, starting with our first pillar, driving brand relevance globally as the clog market share leader. During the quarter, we broadened our relevance across fashion and sport through both new and existing franchises, enabling us to serve a broader range of wearing occasions. Growth in clog iterations such as the Crafted, Crocband, Mellow, and Echo franchises reinforces our conviction that innovation within clogs remains an important lever for future growth. Within Crafted, we saw further momentum as new materializations and seasonally relevant product resonated with consumers, including our Vegan Suede Stitch Clog. Crocband continues to gain momentum globally as we expanded our color options, band innovations, and broadened appeal across both male and female consumers with the addition of our Crocband Runner. Within Mellow, as we spoke about last quarter, we launched our recovery clog, which brings Crocs innovation to the recovery category. Lastly, we expanded the Echo franchise with the launch of Echo 2.0, which delivers strong international performance and broadens our brand's reach to a more athletic, sport-inspired consumer. Collectively, the momentum in these clog iterations illustrates how the consumer is increasingly embracing a broader range of clog silhouettes beyond our iconic Classic Clog franchise. Within our Classic Clog, we remain focused on strengthening and protecting the long-term health of our icon. We continue to invest in compelling brand storytelling, innovation, personalization, and partnerships to drive relevance and keep the Classic Clog at the center of the Crocs ecosystem. Within our kids business, we had strong Classic Clog momentum during the back-to-school season, and will build on this assortment going forward. Next, our second strategic pillar focuses on scaling outside of clogs through category expansion. We have made tremendous progress against our broader diversification strategy, starting with our sandals category. The sandals market represents an estimated $30 billion global addressable market, where we have gained substantial market share, and to date, represent a leading player in this category. Our sandals business continues to grow double digits led by our Miami and Saturday franchises, where we attract new consumers, increase purchase frequency, and gain market share. Sandals represents a year-round business for us as we benefit from warmer weather extending beyond summer, and internationally, we are able to capture demand in counter-seasonal markets. This momentum reinforces our confidence that sandals continues to represent a significant multi-year growth opportunity for the Crocs brand. Next, within our lifestyle franchise, we have seen strong response globally to new innovations, starting with the Ballet Flat. Consumers' strong response to our Ballet Flat demonstrates our ability to capture relevant fashion trends while maintaining the iconic Crocs DNA. Looking ahead, we are testing into lined versions of the Ballet Flat starting in Asia. As we mentioned earlier from a sports lens, we have introduced a closed heel version of our Mellow franchise, giving us another offering within the growing recovery and lifestyle space. As we head into the fourth quarter and key holiday selling season, we believe we are well-positioned to capture demand across a broader range of wearing occasions led by our slippers and lined clogs. More specifically, we are building our Unfurgettable franchise after a successful test season last year, introducing new products such as a platform, the Chalet, and the Après Clog. Another key focus of our product diversification strategy is personalization, which is one of our most powerful drivers of consumer engagement and a key differentiator. For many of our consumers, purchasing Crocs shoes is not a one-time transaction, but the beginning of an ongoing journey of personalization and self-expression. As leaders within the personalization space, we are committed to finding new ways for consumers to express themselves. Following the strong response to our sandal charms test we shared in Q2, we are accelerating plans to expand that offering in 2027. To gain further insights into consumers' personalization journey, we opened a new test and learn store, Crocs by You, in Wuhan, China, that is a destination centered around personalization, where we can see firsthand how consumer loyalty and engagement around personalization can evolve. Next, our third pillar for the Crocs brand focuses on fueling consumer engagement through disruptive social and digital marketing. This quarter, our partnerships business continued to reach a wide range of consumer demographics. Key partnerships in the quarter included Dinoco Cars, Yu-Gi-Oh!, and Pendleton. First, our Dinoco Cars program, which celebrated the 20th anniversary of the Cars franchise, featured our Crocband, as well as a Dinoco Cars collectible. The launch of this partnership was initiated at Disney's D23, which drove significant fan engagement. Dinoco Cars was a top-selling global partnership for our business, based on a long history of success with the Cars franchise. Next, we partnered with Yu-Gi-Oh!, a Japanese multimedia franchise centered on a popular trading card game and anime series, which unlocked broad fan engagement. The partnership was led by iterations on our Classic Clog, paired with an exclusive trading card. Third, we launched a limited edition collaboration with the iconic brand Pendleton. Blending Crocs comfort proposition with vibrant wool colors from Pendleton's Woolen Mills, this collaboration sold out quickly across both our channels as well as Pendleton's, and more importantly, haloed demand on our new Crafted Clog franchise. Turning to our fourth pillar, we are creating compelling consumer experiences across channels. Social commerce remains one of our strongest competitive advantages and is a meaningful growth driver across regions. Our performance in North America across key partners in the space continues to outperform our expectations, building our leadership position and our ability to integrate content creators and commerce in a differentiated way. Internationally, momentum also remains strong with Asia and Europe delivered strong upside during our key shopping events. Notably, this quarter, we maintained our number 1 footwear brand ranking on TikTok Shop in the U.S., U.K., Japan, and most recently, Malaysia. During the quarter, we furthered our testing of AI-enabled shopping experiences across platforms. While early days for agentic shopping, we see it as critical to be actively involved with all major platforms. We have also leaned into the emergence of AI-powered shopping agents and launched Rivet, Crocs proprietary AI-powered shopping agent, on our own website to help consumers discover and evaluate products. We're further experimenting and investing early with emerging shopping experiences, including third-party shopper agents to ensure Crocs is highly discoverable while gaining a deeper understanding of evolving consumer behavior. Finally, our fifth pillar for the Crocs brand focuses on gaining market share internationally. During the third quarter, we saw strong growth across all of our tier 1 international markets. Starting with China, we launched a global marketing campaign around the Echo 2.0 collection, featuring Olympic table tennis gold medalist Fan Zhendong as our brand ambassador. This generated substantial traction in Asia, culminating 40 billion impressions, further accelerating brand awareness while highlighting the power of authentic ambassadors to engage core consumers. In India, growth was broad-based across both direct and wholesale channels as we capitalized on the virality of our Let Them Talk campaign with local cricketer and celebrity KL Rahul, driving demand across both our mainline Echo product as well as our newly introduced Echo 2.0. As we look ahead, we remain confident in the significant international opportunity for the Crocs brand and our ability to leverage product innovation, personalization, and digital leadership to continue to gain market share across key markets. Now turning to HEYDUDE. As we have communicated earlier this year, we expected HEYDUDE to return to growth in the second half of the year. I am pleased to report that we achieved this goal with revenues growing 6% this quarter compared to last year. Over the past year, we've consistently improved the trajectory of the HEYDUDE business, progressing from double-digit declines to now returning to growth. At the same time, we have re-engineered our cost structure and built a stronger financial foundation through higher ASPs, better inventory management, and focused cost efficiencies across the organization. Compared to last year, gross margin increased 350 basis points while SG&A decreased 9%. This performance reinforces our confidence that our three-pillar growth strategy is working, and we believe that this positions HEYDUDE on a stronger financial foundation to unlock sustainable growth. Turning to our first strategic pillar for HEYDUDE. We are laser-focused on our core consumer. During the quarter, we saw clear signs of positive engagement of our core consumer. We launched the campaign Hooked on HEYDUDE, which outperformed prior campaigns and drove meaningful consumer engagement with the brand. Another way we drove engagement during the quarter was through partnerships. During Q3, we launched eight unique collaborations, each one selling out and in turn, reinforcing our ability to deliver culturally relevant product to targeted consumers. Starting with Burlebo, an innovative outdoor lifestyle brand, we built upon the success of our viral Q2 camo collaboration to launch an extended partnership featuring our American Flag Hey2O. This brought Burlebo's distinctive outdoor aesthetic to one of our top silhouettes. Next, we partnered with Buc-ee's, iconic southern travel destination known for its highly engaged and loyal following. This collaboration sold out in just 24 hours and brought Buc-ee's distinctive brand identity and passionate fan base to HEYDUDE in an authentic, regionally relevant way. Collectively, these launches accelerated awareness, amplified consumer demand, and further solidified our go-to-market partnership model. Next, our second pillar focuses on building the core and thoughtfully adding more. We remain focused on optimizing our core assortment while introducing new product innovation to drive growth and broaden consumer reach. Within our core collection, we are growing key iterations of our icons, the Wally and Wendy, through our stretch socks and jersey programs. Most notably, our Wally Braided, which features elevated upper materials, is growing nicely, while our Hey2O, the water-friendly slip-on evolution of the Wally, continues to perform strongly. Beyond our core collection, our sandals business has outperformed our expectations, as well as also diversifying our product offering. Going forward, we see sandals as a strategic growth driver for our business into 2027. Additionally, we have seen success in our work category through leading silhouettes, the Wally CE and the Bradley comp toe boot. For our core consumer, this category is a natural add-on, and we believe we can keep taking meaningful market share in the work segment. As we move into the fourth quarter, we're focused on our seasonal newness across our Easy Boot collection. Our boots franchise has been led by our new Bradley 2 silhouette that gives the consumer an easy on and off boot at a compelling value. Our boots for our female consumer has also driven excitement, led by the Remy. Both of the examples I have just shared were redesigned for comfort and durability, featuring lightweight construction and new tooling. Lastly, heading into the holiday, we're building on our success with seasonal products such as slippers. Moving to our third and last strategic pillar, we are focused on stabilizing the North America marketplace while planting seeds internationally. Our return to growth during the quarter, coupled with international momentum, reflects the meaningful progress we've made against this strategic pillar. Our return to growth in North America was driven by wholesale, which grew 14%, reflecting our progress in building deeper wholesale relationships and driving increased order volumes as partners expand their commitment to our brand. At once, demand was stronger than anticipated as retailers reordered key products and sold through faster than expected. Within our direct-to-consumer business, we are focused on driving higher full price selling and seeing ETVs as well as conversion improve within our retail stores year to date. We are encouraged by the trajectory of HEYDUDE and the way the team is executing across our prioritized strategies. The work we did over the past 12 months to clean up the marketplace, focus on our core consumer, and sharpen our marketing created short-term pressure, but is now translating into a broader base growth opportunity. Building the success of the quarter, we are excited about what lies ahead for HEYDUDE. In many ways, we are just getting started. To conclude my remarks, we remain focused on finishing the year strong by executing the strategies that drive diversified, sustainable growth across our brands, channels, and geographies. These efforts are underpinned by consumer-led innovation, scalable global platforms, and a disciplined financial model. We remain confident in the long-term trajectory of both brands and our ability to generate significant free cash flow and ultimately shareholder value. I will now turn the call over to Patraic.

Patraic Reagan
Thank you, Andrew, and good morning, everyone. We are very pleased with our third quarter performance, which reflects continued progress across both brands and disciplined execution against our strategic priorities. During the quarter, we delivered revenue growth at both Crocs and HEYDUDE brands, with both brands exceeding our expectations. We also expanded adjusted operating margin by 150 basis points compared to last year, as we recognized the benefit from our cost savings initiatives while maintaining disciplined promotional activity. Importantly, as Andrew discussed, the HEYDUDE brand returned to growth. The Crocs brand delivered a record third quarter supported by strong international results and momentum across an increasingly diversified product portfolio. Around the globe, we are playing to win each and every day, running our business with a mindset of ambition, decisiveness, and agility. We are aggressively actioning our strategic priorities, which are focused on innovating on behalf of our consumers around the world, and we are making measurable progress. Now let's move to our results. For the third quarter, we delivered enterprise revenue of just over $1 billion, up 5%, with Crocs brand revenue increasing 4% and HEYDUDE brand revenue increasing 6%. Results were supported by continued strength in direct-to-consumer, particularly international DTC for the Crocs brand, as well as better than expected wholesale performance at HEYDUDE. For the quarter, Crocs brand revenue was $873 million, up 4% year-over-year. International revenue increased approximately 12%, including growth in all of our tier 1 markets. Our international performance was led by the direct-to-consumer channel, up 24%, which included broad-based growth across marketplaces, retail, and our own .com. North America revenue declined approximately 2%, in part driven by the previously communicated impact of our business model shift from the direct-to-consumer to wholesale segment. This shift represents a 270 basis point headwind to the North America DTC channel, reflecting approximately one month of impact to the quarter as we began implementing. Excluding this business model shift, North America DTC is anticipated to be positive for the year. It is important to note that we are increasingly confident in the underlying health of our North America business across all channels and the steps we have taken this year to set the stage for return to growth as we look forward. As Andrew spoke to earlier, growth in the Crocs brand was driven by strong consumer response to our product diversification strategy. This included outperformance within sandals, new clog iterations such as Crafted with new materials, and seasonally relevant product resonating with consumers and new innovations, including the on-trend Ballet Flat. We have built a broad, diverse and durable portfolio of products and will continue to innovate on behalf of the consumer. Moving to HEYDUDE. The HEYDUDE brand delivered revenue of $170 million, up 6% to prior year, exceeding our expectations and marking the brand's return to growth. This represents a significant milestone in the brand's turnaround journey, evidenced by sequential improvement from the trends over the last several quarters. By channel, wholesale was ahead of our expectations, up 14%, supported by higher at once and replenishment orders. D2C was up slightly to prior year, driven by continued marketplace strength despite our planned pullback in promotions. Now, I want to take a moment to highlight HEYDUDE's improvement in inventory composition and full price selling, both of which have improved significantly year to date. Throughout the year, we have been aggressively working to bring inventory levels in channel to be in line with sell-through, and we have made dramatic progress. Within D2C, we have pulled back on discounting across our own.com and marketplaces. Taken together, these are important indicators of the progress we are making to build a healthier, more profitable HEYDUDE business, giving us confidence in the sustainability of our long-term growth moving forward. Now moving to adjusted gross margins. Enterprise adjusted gross margin of 60.3% was up 180 basis points to prior year as we saw gross margin expansion across both Crocs and HEYDUDE brands, driven by disciplined execution of our cost savings initiatives and lower tariffs. We continue to benefit from the cost savings initiatives we implemented during 2025 that focus on supply chain efficiencies, such as simplification of our distribution and negotiations with factories to drive lower product costs. Gross margin expansion was partially offset by planned product mix headwinds resulting from our diversification strategy. Notably, adjusted gross margin excludes $64 million of tariff refunds, which we received during the quarter. Please reference our non-GAAP gross profit and gross margin reconciliation bridge in our earnings press release for more information. Turning to Crocs brand. Adjusted gross margin was 63.4%, up 160 basis points to prior year, driven by lower tariffs, favorable channel mix, and lower product costs, partially offset by product mix as we continue to execute on our diversification strategy. HEYDUDE brand adjusted gross margin was 45.8%, up 350 basis points to prior year, driven by lower tariffs, improved ASPs and product mix. Moving to expenses, adjusted SG&A dollars were $397 million, up 6% to prior year, driven by choiceful DTC channel investments to support revenue growth, in part offset by the benefit from our cost savings initiatives. Adjusted operating margin of 22.3% was up 150 basis points to prior year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share of $3.69 was up 26% to prior year and ahead of our guidance of $3.20- $3.30 per share. Finally, our non-GAAP effective tax rate was 17%. Now turning to a discussion of our strong balance sheet and exceptional cash flow. We ended the quarter with just over $163 million of cash and cash equivalents and approximately $890 million of borrowing capacity on our revolver. Our inventory balance as of September 30th was $413 million, up 4% to prior year, and notably enterprise inventory turns were above our goal of four times on an annualized basis. The power of our business model drives exceptional free cash flow, which provides us with significant flexibility in how we allocate capital and generate shareholder value. During the quarter, we repurchased approximately 2 million shares for $250 million. Another proof point of our commitment to returning capital to shareholders. At the same time, we strengthened our balance sheet. During the quarter, we paid down an additional $21 million of debt and ended the quarter with net leverage at the low end of our target range of 1x- 1.5x . Now moving to the full year 2026 outlook versus prior year. We now expect enterprise revenues to grow approximately 3%, up from our prior guidance range of up 1%-2%, assuming currency rates as of October 26th. Moving on to revenue guidance by brand. For the Crocs brand, we now expect revenue to be up approximately 4% versus our previous guidance range of up 2%-3%, led by international growth. We expect North America revenue to continue to improve versus prior year as we execute our return to growth strategy. Turning to HEYDUDE, we now expect revenue to be approximately flat, an improvement from our previous guidance range of down 2% to down 4%, which reflects our confidence in HEYDUDE's return to growth. We are also raising our bottom line expectations for adjusted diluted earnings per share to now be in the range of $14.45- $14.65, up significantly from our previous guidance range of $13.70 - $14. Consistent with our previous guidance, this range does not assume any impact from future share repurchases. Moving to margin guidance. We continue to expect adjusted gross margin for the year to be up slightly versus last year, driven by our cost-saving efforts, primarily in our supply chain, offset in part by product mix. Adjusted SG&A dollars are implied slightly up to prior year, reflecting investments we are making into growth drivers for the enterprise, offset in part by benefits from our previously announced cost savings programs. Taken together, we are raising our expectations for adjusted operating margin to expand modestly from 22.5%. This excludes a non-GAAP net benefit of approximately $40 million associated with tariff refunds and our cost reduction initiatives. Our GAAP tax, non-GAAP tax, as well as capital expenditure guidance are unchanged for the full year. Now, turning to our fourth quarter outlook versus prior year. For the fourth quarter, we expect enterprise revenue to be up 7%-9%. For the Crocs brand, we expect revenues to be up 6%-8%, and for HEYDUDE, we expect revenues to be up 10%-12%. As Andrew had mentioned, we are quite pleased with the growth trajectories for both of our brands. As a reminder, our year-over-year compares do include anniversarying prior year inventory cleanup actions taken in the North America marketplace. Adjusted operating margin is expected to be approximately 20.5%, which embeds adjusted gross margin up approximately 200 basis points to prior year. Finally, adjusted diluted earnings per share is planned to be in the range of $3.25-$3.45. To close, we are pleased with our continued outperformance this year and the momentum we continue to see across the business. The results we delivered reflect the strength of our brands, broad-based consumer demand, focus on product innovation, and disciplined execution by our teams around the world. As always, we remain focused on driving long-term profitable growth and generating and deploying our exceptional free cash flow to return value to shareholders. At this time, Andrew and I are happy to take your questions. Operator?
